2027-03-26.alt: Good Friday. A day of fasting. The collection of the day is for the Holy Land, as directed by the Holy Father.
2027-03-26.verse: When Jesus had received the wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
theo: On Good Friday the Church stands at the foot of the Cross. The One who entered Jerusalem to the cry of Hosanna is condemned, mocked, scourged, crowned with thorns, and crucified outside the city between two criminals. The Holy One is counted among the wicked. The prophet had seen it long before: “He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities… and by his bruises we are healed” (Isaiah 53:5).

From the Cross Jesus speaks words that the Church treasures. “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.” To the repentant thief: “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.” To his Mother and the beloved disciple: “Woman, here is your son… Here is your mother.” Then the cry of the abandoned: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” And at the end: “It is finished”, and “Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.”

“It is finished” is not a cry of defeat but of completion. The work the Father gave him is accomplished: the true Lamb has been sacrificed, the new covenant sealed in his blood. A soldier pierces his side, “and at once blood and water came out” (John 19:34). The Fathers saw in that blood and water the Eucharist and Baptism, the Church born from the side of Christ as Eve from the side of Adam.

On this day there is no Holy Qurbono in our tradition; the altar is bare because the Lamb himself is offered on the Cross. We venerate the Cross, we keep fast and silence, and we stand with Mary, who did not run away. The wood of shame has become the tree of life. “We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world.”
conn: Isaiah 52:13–53:12 describes the Passion centuries before it happened.
The tree in Eden brought death; the tree of the Cross brings life (Genesis 2:9; Revelation 22:2).
“As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up” (John 3:14; Numbers 21:9).
As Eve was formed from Adam's side, the Church is born from the pierced side of Christ (John 19:34).
altar: Today the altar stands bare and there is no Holy Qurbono, for the one Sacrifice is contemplated on the Cross. Every Qurbono we celebrate makes present this same sacrifice of Calvary; today we simply kneel before it.

fathers: “There flowed from his side water and blood… the symbols of Baptism and the Mysteries. From these two the Church is born… as Eve was formed from the side of Adam” (Catechesis 3, 13–19).
“He stretched out his hands on the Cross, that he might embrace the ends of the world; for Golgotha is the centre of the earth” (Catechetical Lectures 13, 28).
magis: Christ's death is the Paschal sacrifice that accomplishes the definitive redemption of humanity; he offered himself freely.
Mary's union with her Son in the work of salvation is shown at the foot of the Cross.
The Church is born primarily of Christ's total self-giving: from the side of Christ asleep on the Cross.

2027-03-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, crucified for us, we adore you and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Forgive us, remember us in your kingdom, give us your Mother as our mother, and let us die with you to sin, that we may rise with you to life. Amen.

illus: In many Kerala homes on Good Friday the television is switched off, the family eats only kanji, and an old crucifix is placed on the table. The children ask why. A grandmother answers: “Because today Jesus died for you.”

family.explain: Jesus died on the cross because he loves us. Even on the cross he forgave the people who hurt him, and he promised heaven to the thief who asked for mercy.
family.intention: We pray for all who are suffering, and we thank Jesus for his love.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to forgive today?”

catechism: Mary at the foot of the Cross.
kidsaint: One of the men crucified beside Jesus said: “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” Jesus promised: “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” (Later tradition calls him Dismas.) Lesson: it is never too late to turn to Jesus.
term: The day of the Lord's Passion and death. In the Malankara tradition the long service of the Hours is prayed, the Cross is venerated and then laid to rest, recalling the burial of the Lord, and the faithful keep fast.
termMore: Because on this day, through the suffering of Christ, the greatest good was done: the redemption of the world. In Malayalam it is called the Friday of sorrow; both names are true.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we stand at the foot of the Cross. The One who was welcomed with Hosanna on Sunday is today mocked, scourged, crowned with thorns and nailed to a cross between two criminals. Isaiah had seen it: “He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; by his bruises we are healed.”

Listen to his words from the Cross. “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.” He forgives those who are killing him. To the thief who asks to be remembered, he promises: “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” To his Mother and the beloved disciple he says: “Here is your son; here is your mother.” He gives us his own Mother.

And then: “It is finished.” Not “I am finished”, but “It is accomplished.” The work of salvation is complete. The soldier's spear opens his side, and blood and water flow: the Fathers saw there the Eucharist and Baptism, the Church born from the heart of Christ.

Today there is no Qurbono; the altar is bare. We kneel before the Cross, we fast, we keep silence, and we stand with Mary who did not run away. Let each of us forgive someone today, as he forgave. We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Good Friday. Jesus died on the cross. He let it happen because he loves us so much and wanted to take away our sins.
On the cross Jesus forgave the people who hurt him. He told a thief who was sorry: “Today you will be with me in heaven.”
Today let's be quiet, pray, and say sorry to anyone we have hurt. Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for loving me so much!”

intro: Isaiah said of the Servant: he did not open his mouth. Through the long day of his Passion, Jesus speaks little. Today we listen to his silence.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this holy day the Church reads to us the long story of the Passion. And one thing is striking: how little Jesus says. Before the high priest, false witnesses come forward, and he is silent. Before Pilate, the chief priests accuse him, but he gave him no answer, not even to a single charge, so that the governor was greatly amazed (Matthew 27:14).

Isaiah had seen it centuries earlier: he was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth (Isaiah 53:7). His silence is not weakness. It is the silence of the Lamb who has chosen to give his life.

Saint Peter, who had seen it all, explains what that silence means: when he was abused, he did not return abuse; when he suffered, he did not threaten; but he entrusted himself to the one who judges justly (1 Peter 2:23). And Peter adds that Christ left us an example, so that we should follow in his steps (1 Peter 2:21). When we are insulted or treated unjustly, our first instinct is to answer back. The Cross teaches another way: to entrust our cause to God.

On the road to Calvary, Saint Luke tells us, they seized a man, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the country, and they laid the cross on him, and made him carry it behind Jesus (Luke 23:26). He did not choose it. But he became the first to do what every disciple must do: carry the cross behind the Lord. Jeremiah's lament rises from that road: is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? (Lamentations 1:12).

Today there is no Qurbono. Let us keep silence before the Cross. Let us bear one wrong this week without answering back. And let us be a Simon for someone who is carrying a cross too heavy alone: the sick, the grieving, the lonely. We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.

opts.a: The Cross, the tree of life
intro: Through a tree came the fall; through the tree of the Cross came our salvation. The Fathers loved to set the two trees side by side.

sub: The tree in the garden.
Disobedience and its fruit.
One man's obedience undoes it.
points.apply: Name one disobedience you will bring to confession.

sub: Israel bitten in the desert.
Look and live.
The Son of Man lifted up.
points.apply: Look at a crucifix for a few minutes today and simply believe.

sub: The way to the tree was closed.
The Cross opens it again.
Leaves for the healing of the nations.
points.apply: Venerate the Cross today with a kiss or a bow, thanking Christ for opening paradise.

concl: The tree of disobedience brought death; the tree of the Cross brings life.
Looking on the Crucified in faith, we are healed and the way to paradise is open.
opts.resolve: Today I will look on the Cross in faith, confess my disobedience, and thank Christ for opening paradise to me.
homily: Dear friends, the Bible begins in a garden with two trees. In the middle of the garden stood the tree of life, and near it the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (Genesis 2:9). Our first parents listened to the serpent, took the forbidden fruit and ate. From that tree came sin and death, and the way to the tree of life was closed (Genesis 3:24).

Today another tree is raised up outside Jerusalem. The Fathers of the Church loved to set the two side by side. By a tree we fell; by a tree we are raised. Saint Paul says: just as by the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners, so by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous (Romans 5:19). Adam reached out his hand to take; Christ stretches out his hands to give.

In the desert, when the people were bitten by serpents, God told Moses: make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). Jesus himself explained this sign: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life (John 3:14–15). All of us have been bitten by sin. Today we are asked simply to look at the Crucified with faith.

The last pages of the Bible show the tree again. On either side of the river is the tree of life, and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations (Revelation 22:2). Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they will have the right to the tree of life (Revelation 22:14). The Cross has opened the way that was closed in Eden. The wood of shame has become the tree of life.

That is why we venerate the Cross today. When you bow or kiss the cross, you are greeting the tree of life. Let us bring our disobedience to the Lord in confession, look on him with faith, and thank him who on the wood of the Cross opened paradise for us. We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.

intro: Today we stand at the Cross with Mary and John. We do not only remember a death; we contemplate the love that saved the world. Three words guide us: he bore our sins, he cried out in our abandonment, he is the Lamb God provided.

points.h: He was wounded for our transgressions
sub: Isaiah saw the suffering Servant, crushed for our iniquities.
Jesus carries not his own sin but ours; by his wounds we are healed.
“It is finished”: not defeat but accomplishment; the work of salvation is complete.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
When Jesus had received the wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
points.apply: Look at the crucifix today and say: “Lord, you did this for me.”

sub: Jesus prays the words of Psalm 22: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
He enters even our experience of God's absence, so that no one is ever alone again.
The Psalm that begins in anguish ends in trust and praise.
q: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, from the words of my groaning?
And about three o'clock Jesus cried with a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
points.apply: Bring to the Cross someone who feels abandoned, and pray for them by name.

sub: Abraham told Isaac: “God himself will provide the lamb.”
At the Cross God provides his own Son.
A Roman centurion, seeing how Jesus died, confesses: “Truly this man was God's Son!”
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.”
Now when the centurion and those with him, who were keeping watch over Jesus, saw the earthquake and what took place, they were terrified and said, “Truly this man was God's Son!”
points.apply: Venerate the Cross with love today, and keep the fast faithfully.

concl: From the pierced side flowed blood and water: the sacraments of the Church.
Let us remain at the Cross with Mary, in silence and gratitude, waiting in hope for the third day.
